newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Levy said invited to meet Albright.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy said invited to meet Albright.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright has invited Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy to Washington for talks on the crisis in Middle East peacemaking, a Foreign Ministry official said on Tuesday.
The invitation for a Friday meeting coincided with Israeli media reports that the United States was disappointed in its contacts with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on reviving the peace process.
Israel's negotiations with the Palestinians came to a halt when the Jewish state broke ground for a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.

Asked if he could confirm Levy would meet Albright on Friday, the Foreign Ministry official, who asked not to be identified, said: "In principle that is correct, that is to say there is an invitation like that."
The official said Levy had already been set to make a private visit to Florida on Sunday.

A top Palestinian negotiator said any American initiative to revive peace talks was doomed to fail unless it forced Israel to halt construction at the East Jerusalem hill which Palestinians call Jabel Abu Ghneim and Israeli refer to as Har Homa.

"If the U.S. administration wants to create an initiative it has to encompass the end of settlement activity including Jabel Abu Ghneim and to cease treating Israel as a state above the law," Saeb Erekat told Reuters.
Israel also said on Tuesday that Syria was making a more lethal nerve gas and warned Damascus the Jewish state had means many times more destructive at its disposal.

Israeli officials were not immediately available to comment on a report in Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper that Damascus was also close to clinching an arms deal with Russia that would include the acquisition by Syria of more MIG-29 fighter jets.
Levy, while neither directly confirming nor denying he would visit Washington, rejected Israeli media reports Albright wanted to see him because of disappointment at contacts with Netanyahu.
"It is silly and childish because I represent the government's policy and all that will be done will be in line with the policy," Levy told the radio.
He reaffirmed Israel would not stop the 6,500-unit Jerusalem settlement, which has spurred West Bank clashes, nor halt construction in settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Palestinians hope eventually to establish an independent state in the West Bank and Gaza with East Jerusalem as capital. They view settlement building during an interim peace deal phase as pre-empting final peace talks.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said Syria, which last held direct peace negotiations with the Jewish state more than one year ago, was manufacturing a new nerve gas.
"We discovered it a few months ago," Mordechai said.

He was commenting on a report by the Israeli newspaper Haaretz that Syria was manufacturing a nerve gas called VX that acts via the skin and is hard to disperse. It said Syria was preparing warheads for missiles that could deliver the gas.
Levy said the "other side" must understand that "it alone does not control something serious like this but that we also control things that are seven times more serious".
Both Mordechai and Levy called on Syria to return to peace talks that came to a halt under the previous government.

Netanyahu was elected last May after a campaign in which he insisted Israel must keep the Golan Heights, a strategic plateau the Jewish state captured from Syria in 1967. Damascus demands a full Israeli withdrawal.

Israel has declined comment on foreign news reports that it is working on biological and chemical weapons. The Jewish state is widely believed to have around 200 nuclear bombs but neither confirms nor denies it has nuclear capability.
